It is my privilege to present to this August Chamber the proposed 2027 budget of the Department of Finance and its attached agencies.

**[00:41:34.800] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000671)  
Here with us, Mr. Speaker, is the Secretary, the Undersecretary, and all the heads of the attached agencies of the Department of Finance,

**[00:41:42.340] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000672)  
headed, of course, by Secretary Frederick Go.

**[00:41:45.780] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000673)  
Mr. Speaker, Your Honors, the Department of Finance stands as the central engine of our country's economic progress.

**[00:41:51.860] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000674)  
Far

**[00:41:52.520] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000675)  
beyond the mere collection agency, it is tasked with the profound responsibility to architect our nation's fiscal policies,

**[00:42:00.400] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000676)  
empower our local governments toward fiscal independence, and navigate our public sector debt.

**[00:42:06.460] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000677)  
As emphasized in the President's Budget Message for Fiscal Year 2027,

**[00:42:11.400] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000678)  
the government's fiscal strategy remains anchored on strengthening revenue generation

**[00:42:15.800] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000679)  
while ensuring that public expenditures continue to support inclusive and sustainable economic growth.

**[00:42:22.520] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000680)  
The government is working hard to meet the projected national revenue of 5.21 trillion pesos,

**[00:42:29.480] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000681)  
equivalent to 15.7% of GDP in 2027.

**[00:42:34.800] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000682)  
Mr. Speaker, this aggressive revenue mobilization is essential to our fiscal consolidation strategy,

**[00:42:41.360] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000683)  
which seeks to deliberately reduce our national deficit from 5.4% of GDP in 2026 to 5.1% in 2027.

**[00:42:52.520] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000684)  
and steadily down to 3.49% by 2030.

**[00:42:57.560] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000685)  
Mr. Speaker, Your Honors, the Department of Finance's fiscal policy is deeply anchored

**[00:43:02.520] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000686)  
in the Philippine Development Plan 2023-2028 and the Medium-Term Fiscal Framework,

**[00:43:09.620] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000687)  
which seeks to create better jobs, increase people's income, and reduce the poverty rate to a single digit by 2028.

**[00:43:18.900] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000688)  
We are already seeing the results of this strategic plan,

**[00:43:22.520] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000689)  
through the Department's concrete accomplishments,

**[00:43:25.620] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000690)  
particularly, Mr. Speaker, its continued robust revenue collection,

**[00:43:30.580] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000691)  
which grew at an average of 10.54% annually from 2022 to 2025.

**[00:43:37.520] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000692)  
In order to facilitate this, the proposed 2027 fiscal year total expenditure program for the Department of Finance

**[00:43:44.860] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000693)  
is 32.03 billion pesos, consisting of 28.64 billion pesos in new appropriations,

**[00:43:52.520] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000694)  
and 3.40 billion pesos in automatic appropriations.

**[00:43:58.460] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000695)  
This budget represents a 3.5% reduction from the current year,

**[00:44:04.200] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000696)  
demonstrating that the Department is leading by example in fiscal discipline.

**[00:44:10.080] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000697)

of the proposed

**[00:44:20.220] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000700)  
[unclear] 7.2

**[00:44:22.520] Rep. Ziaur-Rahman "Zia" Alonto Adiong** (asr-000701)

**[08:43:58.920] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009326)

that might otherwise

**[08:44:12.220] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009332)  
escape attention.

**[08:44:14.960] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009333)  
Majority and Minority

**[08:44:16.440] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009334)  
may disagree on particular

**[08:44:18.260] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009335)  
items, but

**[08:44:20.060] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009336)  
ultimately, we share

**[08:44:22.660] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009337)

**[08:44:24.180] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009338)  
to make sure

**[08:44:25.980] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009339)  
that the people's

**[08:44:27.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009340)  
money is spent properly.

**[08:44:29.700] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009341)  
And this deliberation showed

**[08:44:33.000] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009342)  
that fiscalization

**[08:44:34.200] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009343)  
can be productive.

**[08:44:36.980] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009344)  
Our questioning did not

**[08:44:38.360] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009345)  
merely identify concerns.

**[08:44:40.720] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009346)  
In several instances,

**[08:44:43.060] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009347)  
it elicited commitments,

**[08:44:45.500] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009348)  
crafted government policy,

**[08:44:47.900] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009349)  
and established timelines

**[08:44:49.560] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009350)  
against which Congress

**[08:44:50.780] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009351)  
can later hold agencies

**[08:44:53.280] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009352)  
accountable.

**[08:44:55.680] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009353)  
There is an old saying,

**[08:44:57.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009354)  
Mr. Speaker,

**[08:44:59.280] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009355)  
Show me

**[08:45:00.000] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009356)  
your budget,

**[08:45:01.000] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009370)  
and I will show you your priorities. The proposed budget is 7.2 trillion pesos. But the 7.2 trillion pesos headline does not tell the whole story.

**[08:45:16.380] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009371)  
Government expects approximately 5.2 trillion in revenues in 2027. Interest payments alone will reach approximately 1.114 trillion. Principal amortization is about 1.59 trillion.

**[08:45:39.220] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009372)  
Perhaps payments are financing transactions and are, strictly speaking,

**[08:45:46.380] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009373)  
not part of the 7.2 trillion expenditure program, but they remain actual obligations of the Treasury.

**[08:45:56.820] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009374)  
Taken together, that service reaches approximately 2.7 trillion, equivalent to almost 52 for every 100 pesos of projected government revenue.

**[08:46:13.520] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009375)  
52 pesos.

**[08:46:16.380] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009376)  
Then, government must provide for the national tax allotment, salaries, pensions, statutory contributions, and other mandatory expenditures.

**[08:46:30.780] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009377)  
So while we speak of a 7.2 trillion budget, the amount over which government actually has room to make choices is much smaller.

**[08:46:44.780] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009378)  
The amount of 2.6 trillion.

**[08:46:46.380] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009379)  
About 36 percent of the 7.2 trillion budget.

**[08:46:53.700] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009380)  
Kung ganoon, pagkatapos bayaran ang utang at ang mga obligasyon, hindi na maaring pagpaliban, mas maliit ang perang tunay nating mapapagpasyahan.

**[08:47:09.200] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009381)  
That is fiscal reality behind this budget.

**[08:47:12.680] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009382)  
This budget will also operate in a difficult economic environment.

**[08:47:20.700] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009383)  
GDP grew by only 2.3 percent in the second quarter of 2026, after growth of 2.8 percent in the first quarter.

**[08:47:32.640] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009384)  
Industry contracted by 2.4 percent, while gross capital formation fell by 9.2%.

**[08:47:42.680] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009385)  
At the same time, inflation remained high at 6.1 percent in August.

**[08:47:52.740] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009386)  
For the bottom 30 percent of Filipino households, inflation was even higher at 8.2 percent.

**[08:48:03.300] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009387)  
These numbers matter because slower growth limits income and employment opportunities.

**[08:48:12.480] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009388)  
While

**[08:48:13.100] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009399)  
Inflation reduces what those incomes can buy.

**[08:48:18.580] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009400)  
Para sa ordinaryong pamilya, simply lang ang ibig sabihin nito, mas mabagal na paglago ng kita, pero mas mabilis ang pagtaas ng presyo ng mga bilihin at serbisyo.

**[08:48:35.900] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009401)  
This is why the quality of government spending matters as much as its size.

**[08:48:42.680] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009402)  
The minority recognizes the need for fiscal consolidation. Under the government's medium-term framework, the deficit is expected to decline from approximately 5.4% of GDP in 2026 to 3.5% by 2030.

**[08:49:07.760] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009403)  
But the revenues remain broadly around 15-16% of GDP, while disbursements decline from approximately 21.2% to 19.1%.

**[08:49:26.080] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009404)  
Much of the adjustments, therefore, comes from expenditure restraint.

**[08:49:31.280] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009405)  
There is nothing wrong with spending discipline.

**[08:49:36.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009406)  
Government shall eliminate waste, duplication, and projects that cannot be implemented.

**[08:49:46.400] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009407)  
But restraint should protect essential investments in people and productive capacity.

**[08:49:54.600] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009408)  
Education illustrates the pressure on our fiscal space.

**[08:49:58.780] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009409)  
The proposed DepEd budget is approximately P976 billion.

**[08:50:06.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009410)  
While interest payments alone are approximately P1.114 trillion.

**[08:50:14.260] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009411)  
We therefore spend about P138 billion more on interest than on the entire Department of Education.

**[08:50:25.100] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009412)  
Education sector spending is approximately 3.99% of GDP,

**[08:50:33.180] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009413)  
compared with roughly...

**[08:50:36.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009414)  
4.36% under the fiscal year of 2026 GAA.

**[08:50:42.720] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009415)  
The classroom shortage remains substantial.

**[08:50:49.280] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009416)  
Social protection deserves attention.

**[08:50:53.320] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009417)  
The 4Ps allocation moves from approximately P113 billion to P99.08 billion.

**[08:51:04.840] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009418)  
AICS...

**[08:51:06.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009419)  
...from approximately P63.9 billion to P33.29 billion.

**[08:51:12.560] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009420)  
And the supplementary feeding program for approximately P9.56 billion to P6.36 billion.

**[08:51:23.260] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009421)  
There may be a valid program and targeting reasons for these adjustments.

**[08:51:30.320] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009422)  
But with inflation among our poorest households,

**[08:51:33.820] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009423)  
at 82.2%,

**[08:51:37.140] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009424)  
these reductions deserve careful monitoring.

**[08:51:42.280] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009425)  
Kapag limitado ang pera,

**[08:51:45.700] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009426)  
dapat unang protektahan ang mga programang

**[08:51:50.240] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009427)  
may pinakamalaking epekto

**[08:51:52.520] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009428)  
sa mga pamilyang

**[08:51:54.300] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009429)  
pinakamaliliit ang kakayahang

**[08:51:57.180] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009430)  
harapin ang pagtaas ng presyo.

**[08:52:00.760] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009431)  
Our colleagues in the minority

**[08:59:30.460] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009658)  
to provide affordable

**[08:59:32.460] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009659)  
capital to entrepreneurs.

**[08:59:34.460] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009660)  
His point is simple.

**[08:59:36.460] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009661)  
Public funds

**[08:59:38.460] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009662)  
should translate into education,

**[08:59:40.460] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009663)  
accessible healthcare,

**[08:59:42.460] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009664)  
and opportunities for

**[08:59:44.460] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009665)  
people to earn

**[08:59:46.460] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009666)  
a sustainable livelihood.

**[08:59:48.460] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009667)  
Representative

**[08:59:50.460] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009668)  
Percy Cenda?a

**[08:59:52.460] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009669)  
of Agbayan Partylist

**[08:59:54.460] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009670)  
called attention to the proposed

**[08:59:56.460] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009671)  
zero funding for the EDSA

**[08:59:58.460] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009672)  
Carousel Service

**[08:59:59.540] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009673)  
contracting, and fuel subsidy programs which directly affect commuters and PUV drivers and operators.

**[09:00:10.260] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009674)  
He likewise joined the call for the remittance of earmarked revenues intended for universal healthcare

**[09:00:17.420] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009675)  
and adequate funding for field health.

**[09:00:21.760] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009676)  
Representative J.C. Abalos of 4Ps Partylist raised the implementation concerns

**[09:00:29.000] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009677)  
regarding the community-based monitoring system.

**[09:00:32.700] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009678)  
The proposed CBMS budget is about 5.062 billion, yet 4.92 billion, or 97%, is lodged in the Central Office,

**[09:00:47.700] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009679)  
while 16 regions and BARMM share only 130 million.

**[09:00:53.500] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009680)  
More importantly, 59,462 families.

**[09:00:59.000] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009681)  
In the 4Ps set, 12 waitlists remain unmatched with CBMS data, some since 2023.

**[09:01:11.260] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009682)  
Representative Audrey Zubiri of the 3rd District of Bukidnon raised the continued funding shortfall

**[09:01:20.020] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009683)  
under the Sugarcane Industry Development Act.

**[09:01:23.300] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009684)  
The law provides for an aggregate of 2 billion annually.

**[09:01:29.000] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009685)  
Yet, approximately 1.020 billion was appropriated in the 2026 GA.

**[09:01:40.020] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009686)  
Her concern raises a broader principle.

**[09:01:42.640] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009687)  
When Congress creates a program and provides a statutory funding mandate,

**[09:01:50.780] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009688)  
annual budgets should give meaningful effect to that commitment.

**[09:01:56.460] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009689)  
Representative Presley De Jesus,

**[09:01:59.000] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009690)  
of PHILRECA Partylist,

**[09:02:02.060] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009691)  
called for stronger support for total missionary electrification,

**[09:02:07.420] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009692)  
total and missionary electrification,

**[09:02:10.900] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009693)  
noting that proposed budgetary support for NEA

**[09:02:13.760] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009694)  
declines from 10.134 billion in 2026

**[09:02:22.260] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009695)  
to 6.486 billion in 2027.

**[09:02:29.000] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009696)  
While many electric cooperatives still need to expand service

**[09:02:35.760] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009697)  
and rehabilitate aging distribution systems.

**[09:02:41.780] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009698)  
He likewise raised the adequacy of the 2.001 billion allocation

**[09:02:49.020] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009699)  
for missionary electrification,

**[09:02:51.700] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009700)  
particularly as higher fuel costs affect national power corporation,

**[09:02:57.060] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009701)  
Small Power Utilities Group

**[09:02:59.000] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009702)  
operations in off-grid communities.

**[09:03:03.000] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009703)  
He also emphasized the need to strengthen ERC's regulatory capacity

**[09:03:09.780] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009704)  
so that government addresses not only price spikes for temporary interventions,

**[09:03:15.860] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009705)  
but their underlying causes, supply shortages, inadequate reserves,

**[09:03:22.900] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009706)  
generation outages, and transmission congestion.

**[09:03:27.820] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009707)  
The concern,

**[09:03:29.000] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009708)  
the over-reliability and affordability was reinforced

**[09:03:34.000] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009709)  
by Representative Sergio Dagooc of APEC Partylist,

**[09:03:39.000] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009710)  
who focused particularly on the continuing energy problems in the Visayas.

**[09:03:45.820] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009711)  
He emphasized that generation shortages,

**[09:03:50.220] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009712)  
inadequate reserves and ancillary services,

**[09:03:53.820] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009713)  
transmission congestion,

**[09:03:56.280] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009714)  
and line rental charges

**[09:03:57.700] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009715)  
must be addressed

**[09:03:59.000] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009716)  
as one systemic problem.

**[09:04:02.880] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009717)  
He likewise called for the rehabilitation of the Agus Pulangi hydro power complex

**[09:04:10.500] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009718)  
while retaining government ownership and control,

**[09:04:14.820] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009719)  
and a reassessment of a limited strategic role

**[09:04:18.620] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009720)  
for NPC in emergency reserves and ancillary services,

**[09:04:24.040] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009721)  
and consideration of a temporary,

**[09:04:29.000] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009722)  
rule-based VAT shock absorber during extraordinary electricity and fuel price increases.

**[09:04:37.880] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009723)  
His concern reminds us that energy policy is also economic policy.

**[09:04:46.560] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009724)  
High power and fuel costs eventually find their way into transportation, food, production, and inflation.

**[09:04:56.700] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009725)  
Representative Bong Suntay of the 4th District of Quezon City emphasized

**[09:05:03.080] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009726)  
that major appropriations must produce measurable results.

**[09:05:08.740] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009727)  
He pointed to the P191.285 billion proposed

**[09:05:15.040] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009728)  
for the Metro Manila Subway and North-South Commuter Railway,

**[09:05:20.500] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009729)  
stressing that rail spending must ultimately be measured

**[09:05:25.820] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009730)  
by working trains and improved mobility.

**[09:05:29.360] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009731)  
He likewise called for health spending

**[09:05:31.700] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009732)  
to reduce the still substantial out-of-pocket burden

**[09:05:35.980] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009733)  
on Filipino families

**[09:05:38.420] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009734)  
and for government to maintain a credible fiscal plan

**[09:05:42.520] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009735)  
should revenues or economic growth fall below assumptions.

**[09:05:49.540] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009736)  
These concerns differ in subject,

**[09:05:53.060] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009737)  
but they reflect the same question before us:

**[09:05:55.820] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009738)  
With limited resources, where can government spending make the greatest difference?

**[09:06:05.960] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009739)  
That question applies equally to our investments in infrastructure.

**[09:06:12.960] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009740)  
Mr. Speaker, even with limited fiscal space,

**[09:06:18.500] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009741)  
we should protect infrastructure that can expand the economy

**[09:06:23.200] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009742)  
and improve national connectivity.

**[09:06:25.820] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009743)  
Our interpellation yesterday on the DPWH budget

**[09:06:32.340] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009744)  
produced concrete commitments on the Sorsogon-Samar Link Bridge.

**[09:06:39.080] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009745)  
We were informed that the government's 130 million

**[09:06:43.380] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009746)  
for the feasibility study will be complemented

**[09:06:48.020] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009747)  
by approximately 500 million from ADB,

**[09:06:51.380] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009748)  
completing the estimated 650 million funding requirement.

**[09:06:57.320] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009756)  
Bidding is expected to begin this November

**[09:07:00.060] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009757)  
with the study taking about one year.

**[09:07:07.320] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009758)  
Detailed engineering is targeted for 2028

**[09:07:10.260] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009759)  
followed by civil works bidding in 2028 or early 2029.

**[09:07:15.620] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009760)  
If the project proves feasible

**[09:07:18.260] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009761)  
and the timetable is followed,

**[09:07:21.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009762)  
completion could be around 2025

**[09:07:24.280] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009763)  
or 2036.

**[09:07:26.920] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009764)  
This is significant because

**[09:07:29.020] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009765)  
Secretary Vince Dixon cited an estimated

**[09:07:31.300] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009766)  
42% economic rate of return

**[09:07:35.240] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009767)  
for the project and inform us

**[09:07:37.840] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009768)  
of a strong interest

**[09:07:39.200] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009769)  
from development partners and investors.

**[09:07:55.360] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009770)  
This also should be a challenge to NEDA,

**[09:07:59.300] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009771)  
DEPDev and DEPDev.

**[09:08:03.300] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009772)  
ADB and higher development partners appear willing

**[09:08:08.300] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009773)  
to support the mega projects

**[09:08:11.300] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009774)  
when the economic case is strong.

**[09:08:13.300] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009775)  
Let us identify other major infrastructure projects

**[09:08:18.300] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009776)  
with high economic rates of return,

**[09:08:21.300] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009777)  
subject them to rigorous feasibility studies,

**[09:08:24.300] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009778)  
and bring them to the table.

**[09:08:25.300] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009779)  
If the project is a viable project to ADB,

**[09:08:27.300] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009780)  
JICA, Korea, and other development partners,

**[09:08:31.240] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009781)  
Kung mataas ang economic return

**[09:08:34.240] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009782)  
at may handang tumulong sa financing,

**[09:08:36.240] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009783)  
hanapin natin ang mga proyektong ito

**[09:08:39.240] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009784)  
at simulan natin.

**[09:08:41.240] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009785)  
May pondo na,

**[09:08:43.240] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009786)  
may timetable pa.

**[09:08:45.240] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009787)  
Ang mas mahalaga ngayon

**[09:08:47.240] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009788)  
ay matupad ang mga commitment na ito.

**[09:08:49.240] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009789)  
The vision, however,

**[09:08:51.240] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009790)  
should extend beyond Sorsogon and Samar.

**[09:08:53.240] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009791)  
For the

**[09:08:55.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009792)  
for the Southern Leyte-Surigao Link,

**[09:08:58.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009793)  
350 million has been identified

**[09:09:01.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009794)  
for the feasibility study

**[09:09:03.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009795)  
with DPWH negotiating with ADB

**[09:09:08.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009796)  
for additional funding required.

**[09:09:11.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009797)  
During the same interpellation,

**[09:09:14.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009798)  
we also obtained commitments

**[09:09:17.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009799)  
to pursue funding for three additional inter-island links,

**[09:09:21.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009800)  
Maasin, Southern Leyte,

**[09:09:24.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009801)  
to Lapinig Island,

**[09:09:26.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009802)  
to Ubay, to Bohol,

**[09:09:28.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009803)  
Getafe, Bohol,

**[09:09:30.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009804)  
to Cordoba, Cebu,

**[09:09:32.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009805)  
and Santander, Cebu,

**[09:09:35.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009806)  
to Sibulan, Negros.

**[09:09:37.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009807)  
The DPWUH indicated

**[09:09:39.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009808)  
that these projects could secure

**[09:09:42.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009809)  
funding in the next budget

**[09:09:45.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009810)  
and through development partners or investors

**[09:09:48.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009811)  
with the Bohol-Cebu connection already studied

**[09:09:51.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009812)  
by the department,

**[09:09:53.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009813)  
and identified as a priority.

**[09:09:57.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009814)  
We should also include

**[09:09:59.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009815)  
the Camarines Sur-Catanduanes Inter-Island Connectivity Project

**[09:10:05.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009816)  
or the Friendship Bridge

**[09:10:08.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009817)  
being pushed by Representative Leo Rodriguez of Catanduanes,

**[09:10:12.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009818)  
envisioned as a long-span bridge connecting Catanduanes

**[09:10:17.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009819)  
to mainland Bicol.

**[09:10:19.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009820)  
The project already has around 80 million

**[09:10:22.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009821)  
in the 2026 GAA for feasibility study.

**[09:10:25.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009822)  
It belongs to the same larger vision

**[09:10:28.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009823)  
using strategic inter-island links

**[09:10:31.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009824)  
to connect communities that geography

**[09:10:34.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009825)  
has long kept apart.

**[09:10:37.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009826)  
Taken together,

**[09:10:39.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009827)  
these proposed links

**[09:10:41.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009828)  
could form part of a more integrated

**[09:10:43.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009829)  
inter-island transport network

**[09:10:46.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009830)  
across the Philippine archipelago,

**[09:10:48.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009831)  
connecting Catanduanes to mainland Bicol,

**[09:10:52.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009832)  
Luzon to Samar, Samar to Leyte,

**[09:10:55.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009833)  
Leyte to Mindanao,

**[09:10:57.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009834)  
while establishing additional fixed links

**[09:11:00.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009835)  
from Leyte to Bohol,

**[09:11:02.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009836)  
Bohol to Cebu, Cebu to Negros,

**[09:11:05.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009837)  
and eventually Negros to Panay,

**[09:11:08.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009838)  
complementing the Panay-Guimaras-Negros Island Bridges project.

**[09:11:13.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009839)  
In a period of slow economic growth,

**[09:11:16.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009840)  
these are the kinds of transformative projects

**[09:11:19.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009841)  
worth carefully pursuing.

**[09:11:21.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009842)  
Projects that can shorten travel time,

**[09:11:24.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009843)  
lower logistics costs,

**[09:11:26.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009844)  
open new markets,

**[09:11:28.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009845)  
bring communities closer together,

**[09:11:31.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009846)  
and ultimately expand the country's productive capacity.

**[09:11:35.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009847)  
As this representation has said

**[09:11:38.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009848)  
during the interpellation,

**[09:11:40.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009849)  
we bring our people to their destination faster.

**[09:11:45.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009850)  
We can bring our patients faster to our hospitals.

**[09:11:49.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009851)  
We can move

**[09:11:50.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009852)  
our goods faster,

**[09:11:51.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009853)  
and we can bring our families closer together.

**[09:11:56.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009854)  
But connectivity is not only an economic issue.

**[09:12:00.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009855)  
In an archipelagic country,

**[09:12:03.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009856)  
the same infrastructure that moves people and goods

**[09:12:06.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009857)  
also strengthens our ability

**[09:12:09.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009858)  
to respond to disasters,

**[09:12:11.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009859)  
move resources,

**[09:12:13.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009860)  
and secure our territory.

**[09:12:15.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009861)  
This brings us to another concern

**[09:12:17.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009862)  
raised during the budget deliberations

**[09:12:19.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009863)  
the need to strengthen our eastern seaboard.

**[09:12:24.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009864)  
Our eastern coast is not only an economic corridor,

**[09:12:27.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009865)  
it is also a strategic frontier.

**[09:12:30.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009866)  
In recent weeks,

**[09:12:32.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009867)  
the AFP confirmed monitoring foreign vessels

**[09:12:35.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009868)  
passing off the coast of eastern Samar.

**[09:12:38.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009869)  
The AFP assessed that particular passage

**[09:12:41.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009870)  
as non-threatening and consistent with navigation

**[09:12:45.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009871)  
through a normal shipping route.

**[09:12:47.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009872)  
We accept that professional assessment,

**[09:12:50.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009873)  
but it also reminds us of something basic.

**[09:12:55.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009874)  
Our defense posture cannot only be westward.

**[09:13:00.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009875)  
The Philippines is an archipelago.

**[09:13:04.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009876)  
Our eastern approaches face Pacific

**[09:13:09.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009877)  
and cover a vast maritime area.

**[09:13:12.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009878)  
The AFP's comprehensive archipelagic defense concept itself

**[09:13:16.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009879)  
recognizes the need to defend our entire maritime domain,

**[09:13:21.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009880)  
including our exclusive economic zones

**[09:13:24.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009881)  
and vital sea lanes.

**[09:13:26.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009882)  
Consequently,

**[09:13:28.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009883)  
Representative Christopher Sheen Gonzales

**[09:13:31.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009884)  
of the Lone District of Eastern Samar proposes

**[09:13:34.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009885)  
for the need to strengthen the country's defense posture

**[09:13:37.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009886)  
along eastern seaboard.

**[09:13:39.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009887)  
As our forces modernizes,

**[09:13:41.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009888)  
he called for greater investments

**[09:13:44.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009889)  
in maritime domain awareness,

**[09:13:46.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009890)  
radar and surveillance,

**[09:13:49.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009891)  
naval and air capacities,

**[09:13:51.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009892)  
and strategic facilities

**[09:13:54.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009893)  
along our Pacific coast

**[09:13:56.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009894)  
that will enable our forces

**[09:13:58.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009895)  
to effectively monitor and respond

**[09:14:01.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009896)  
when necessary.

**[09:14:03.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009897)  
This is not about identifying any country

**[09:14:07.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009898)  
as an enemy.

**[09:14:09.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009899)  
It is simply responsible national defense.

**[09:14:14.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009900)  
Kung pinapalakas

**[09:14:16.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009901)  
natin ang depensa sa kaunlaran.

**[09:14:19.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009902)  
Hindi dapat pabayaan ang silangan.

**[09:14:22.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009903)  
Ang isang kapuluan ay dapat may kakayahang bantayan

**[09:14:26.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009904)  
ang kanyang mga hangganan.

**[09:14:30.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009905)  
The bridges and transport links

**[09:14:32.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009906)  
we have discussed also have strategic dimension.

**[09:14:35.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009907)  
Better ports, roads, bridges, and logistics networks

**[09:14:41.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009908)  
strengthen not only commerce

**[09:14:44.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009909)  
but also disaster response, humanitarian assistance, and national resilience.

**[09:14:51.760] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009910)  
A connected Eastern Seaboard should therefore be a part of a broader national strategy.

**[09:15:00.000] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009911)  
We must protect it economically, secure it adequately, and ensure that development reaches the regions that have historically remained farthest from the centers of growth.

**[09:15:14.300] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009912)  
And that brings us to another principle that should guide this budget – regional equity.

**[09:15:20.960] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009913)  
Earlier, House Policy Research found that budget shares of Visayas and Mindanao have historically fallen below the shares of the country's poor population.

**[09:15:36.600] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009914)  
Large appropriations classified as nationwide or central office expenditures also make geographic distribution difficult to determine at enactment.

**[09:15:48.220] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009915)  
We are not asking for equal amounts for every region.

**[09:15:53.280] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009916)  
Allocations should reflect population, poverty, infrastructure, infrastructure gaps, disaster exposure, and geographic isolation.

**[09:16:06.640] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009917)  
Hindi dapat maging hadlang sa pag-unlad ang pagiging malayo sa sintro ng bansa.

**[09:16:13.700] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009918)  
We acknowledge one important reform in this budget.

**[09:16:18.220] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009919)  
Unprogrammed appropriations have been reduced approximately 112 billion or only 1.6% of the expenditure program.

**[09:16:30.680] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009920)  
That is welcome.

**[09:16:33.240] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009921)  
But transparency must also extend to program appropriations.

**[09:16:37.860] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009922)  
Congress should know, as far as practicable, the project, location, beneficiary, and purpose of the funds it appropriates.

**[09:16:48.660] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009923)  
Post-enactment discretion through lump sums, realignments, and release conditions should remain limited and transparent.

**[09:16:58.640] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009924)  
Kung ang kongreso ang may power of the purse dapat malinaw sa atin kung saan papunta ang pera sa oras na aprobahan natin ang budget.

**[09:17:10.020] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009925)  
And accountability should continue after enactment.

**[09:17:14.400] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009926)  
Indeed, an appropriation is not an

**[09:17:18.220] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009927)  
accomplishment.

**[09:17:19.480] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009928)  
What matters is what kind is what was actually implemented and whether it improved people's lives.

**[09:17:28.140] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009929)  
Representative Robert Nazal of [unclear] also cautioned against unlawful or manufactured savings.

**[09:17:38.720] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009930)  
Unspent funds should not automatically become savings.

**[09:17:42.780] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009931)  
And projects should not be delayed.

**[09:17:46.920] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009932)  
Merely to create funds

**[09:17:48.220] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009933)  
for transfer elsewhere.

**[09:17:51.920] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009934)  
Every declaration of savings must have a clear legal basis, proper documentation, and accountability.

**[09:18:02.360] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009935)  
Relatedly, Representative Edgar Erice of the 2nd District of Caloocan raised an important constitutional concern regarding the local government support fund.

**[09:18:16.120] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009936)  
and amount of discretion

**[09:18:18.220] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009937)  
that may remain after Congress approves the budget.

**[09:18:23.520] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009938)  
The Supreme Court has upheld the LGU as a valid appropriation where it has sufficiently defined purpose and adequate standards governing its implementation.

**[09:18:36.980] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009939)  
But this concern deserves attention.

**[09:18:39.680] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009940)  
Kung pagkatapos nating aprobahan ng budget, saka pa lamang malalaman kung aling LGU ang makakakuha,

**[09:18:48.220] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009941)  
magkano ang makakatanggap at kung anong proyekto ang pupunduhan,

**[09:18:51.780] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009942)  
Congress must carefully examine whether it has sufficiently exercised its own power of appropriation.

**[09:19:00.440] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009943)  
The issue is not whether we should assist our LGUs.

**[09:19:06.000] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009944)  
We should.

**[09:19:06.720] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009945)  
The issue is whether the GAA itself provides clear and objective standards

**[09:19:13.520] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009946)  
so that the allocation of billions of pesos in local government

**[09:19:18.220] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009947)  
support remains consistent with Congress' constitutional power of the purse.

**[09:19:25.920] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009948)  
Madam Speaker,

**[09:19:27.980] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009949)  
the minority recognizes the good provisions of this measure.

**[09:19:32.560] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009950)  
We recognize the reduction of the unprogrammed operations.

**[09:19:36.640] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009951)  
We recognize the need for fiscal discipline.

**[09:19:39.980] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009952)  
We recognize the programs and infrastructure investments that can contribute to growth.

**[09:19:46.360] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009953)  
And we appreciate

**[09:19:47.620] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009966)  
the majority's willingness to subject this budget to sustained scrutiny, but our reservations remain.

**[09:19:58.160] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009967)  
The fiscal choices before us are therefore difficult.

**[09:20:03.760] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009968)  
Economic growth has slowed, inflation continues to weigh most heavily on poorer households,

**[09:20:11.480] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009969)  
and substantial share of government revenues is already committed to debt service and other mandatory obligations.

**[09:20:22.080] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009970)  
Against this backdrop, the real measure of 7.2 trillion budget is not its size,

**[09:20:31.040] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009971)  
but the choices we make with the fiscal space that remains.

**[09:20:36.760] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009972)  
Whether we spend it efficiently,

**[09:20:41.480] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009973)  
direct it where it matters most,

**[09:20:44.540] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009974)  
and invest it in ways that strengthen our capacity to grow.

**[09:20:50.880] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009975)  
I began by saying, show me your budget, I will show you your priorities.

**[09:20:57.780] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009976)  
After these deliberations, I would add only this.

**[09:21:02.460] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009977)  
Ipakita natin kung saan napunta ang bawat pesong kaya pa nating pagpasyahan,

**[09:21:09.640] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009978)  
at ipakita natin ang resulta.

**[09:21:12.380] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009979)  
The final test of this budget will not be found in these pages.

**[09:21:18.640] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009980)  
It will be found in the lives of our people.

**[09:21:22.360] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009981)  
Kung dahil sa budget na ito,

**[09:21:23.780] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009982)  
ay mas maraming Pilipino ang magkakaroon ng disinting trabaho,

**[09:21:29.300] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009983)  
mapayapang tahanan, magandang kinabukasan para sa kanilang mga anak,

**[09:21:35.260] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009984)  
at pagkakataong umasinso sa sariling pagsisikap,

**[09:21:41.240] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009985)  
then,

**[09:21:41.480] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009986)  
we will have done our duty.

**[09:21:44.820] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009987)  
Sapagkat,

**[09:21:46.280] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009988)  
ang tunay na pagunlad,

**[09:21:48.580] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009989)  
ay kapag

**[09:21:49.500] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009990)  
ang mga kababayan natin

**[09:21:52.640] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009991)  
ay nabubuhay ng marangal,

**[09:21:56.520] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009992)  
may tiwala sa sarili,

**[09:21:58.600] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009993)  
at may pagmamalaking sabihin,

**[09:22:02.200] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009994)  
Pilipino ako.

**[09:22:03.700] Minority Leader Marcelino C. Libanan** (asr-009995)  
Maraming salamat, Madam Speaker.

**[09:22:05.280] Committee member** (asr-009996)  
[applause]

**[09:22:06.280] Committee member** (asr-009997)  
[applause]

**[09:22:08.760] Deputy Speaker Mercedes K. Alvarez** (asr-009998)  
Majority Leader.

**[09:22:12.360] Committee member** (asr-009999)  
[applause]

**[09:22:22.240] Deputy Speaker Mercedes K. Alvarez** (asr-010000)  
Majority Leader.

**[09:22:23.980] Rep. Johanne Monich G. Bautista** (asr-010001)  
Madam Speaker,

**[09:22:24.860] Rep. Johanne Monich G. Bautista** (asr-010002)  
I move to recognize Representative Antonio L. Tinio

**[09:22:28.800] Rep. Johanne Monich G. Bautista** (asr-010003)  
of ACT-Teachers Party List

**[09:22:30.500] Rep. Johanne Monich G. Bautista** (asr-010004)  
for his manifestation.

**[09:22:32.080] Deputy Speaker Mercedes K. Alvarez** (asr-010005)  
Representative Antonio Tinio is recognized for his manifestation.

**[09:22:36.880] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010006)  
Maraming Salamat, Madam Speaker.

**[09:22:40.140] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010007)  
Madam Speaker,

**[09:22:41.420] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010008)  
Mga kasamahan sa Kongreso, ang pinakamahalagang tanong sa ating sampung araw na debate at interpelasyon sa pambansang budget para sa 2027 ay hindi kung magkano.

**[09:22:57.840] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010009)  
Hindi mga numero at statistika, kundi para kanino? Para kanino ang budget na ito?

**[09:23:07.240] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010010)  
Sino ang pangunahing pinagsisilbihan ng budget? Sino ang pangunahing makikinabang?

**[09:23:17.040] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010011)  
Sinasabi ng Malacanang, para sa bayan, this is a people's budget, they say. We say to that, really? Talaga ba?

**[09:23:28.100] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010012)  
The right reply to that is, who are these people you speak of?

**[09:23:36.300] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010013)  
Ang pambansang budget.

**[09:23:37.240] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010014)  
Ang pambansang budget ay salamin ng pambansang patakaran.

**[09:23:41.800] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010015)  
Sabi ng presidente at mga economic managers, hindi na mahirap na bansa ang Pilipinas. Upper middle income country na raw tayo.

**[09:23:52.600] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010016)  
Pero, sabi ng ordinaryong Pilipino, di ko ramdam. Bakit ganon?

**[09:23:59.060] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010017)  
For decades, the national budget has faithfully supported one set of policies.

**[09:24:07.240] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010018)  
Often called neoliberal or free market policies. Ito po yung privatization, deregulation, and liberalization.

**[09:24:16.580] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010019)  
Under these policies, the things a nation needs just to function are now owned by a handful of families and conglomerates.

**[09:24:27.160] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010020)  
Energy. Oil and gas. Electricity. Water. Telecommunications. Our expressways.

**[09:24:37.240] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010021)  
Airports. Seaports. Dating nasa kamay ng gobyerno, ngayon, malalaking profit centers pinagkikitaan ng iilan.

**[09:24:49.740] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010022)  
Lumago ang ekonomiya. At sila ang pangunahing nakikinabang.

**[09:24:55.300] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010023)  
Ano ang resulta? Mahal na serbisyo. Mataas na presyo. Mahal na kuryente. Mahal na tubig. Mahal na bigas.

**[09:25:07.240] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010024)  
At pambihirang yaman para sa iilang oligarko.

**[09:25:12.000] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010025)  
Hindi na lang mga bilyonaryo. Mga trilyonaryo na ang mga pinakamayamang Pilipino.

**[09:25:20.420] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010026)  
Razon, Ramon Ang, Pangilinan, Aboitiz. Yan lang ang ilan sa mga pangunahing nakikinabang sa economic policies and environment na sinusustentuhan ng pambansang budget.

**[09:25:35.900] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010027)  
Samantala, sino ang pumapasan, pinipiga, at nagbabayad?

**[09:25:42.780] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010028)  
Ang mga small and medium businesses na gipit dahil sa

**[09:25:48.400] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010029)  
mataas na kuryente, mataas

**[09:25:50.540] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010030)  
na interes sa loans,

**[09:25:52.440] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010031)  
kompetisyon mula sa

**[09:25:54.360] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010032)  
murang imported goods due

**[09:25:56.460] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010033)  
to liberalization.

**[09:25:58.280] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010034)  
Ang Filipino middle class

**[09:26:00.340] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010035)  
kasama ang mga

**[09:26:02.220] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010036)  
profesional na mababa ang kita

**[09:26:04.600] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010037)  
underpaid

**[09:26:06.080] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010038)  
and overtaxed.

**[09:26:08.140] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010039)  
Milyon-milyon sa kanila

**[09:26:09.440] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010040)  
ang nangibang bansa bilang

**[09:26:12.060] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010041)  
OFW dahil

**[09:26:14.220] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010042)  
wala silang maasahan

**[09:26:15.700] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010043)  
sa ating ekonomiya.

**[09:26:17.340] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010044)  
At higit sa lahat

**[09:26:19.340] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010045)  
ang malawak na hanay

**[09:26:21.460] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010046)  
ng mamamayan.

**[09:26:23.920] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010047)  
Ano ang para sa kanila?

**[09:26:25.920] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010048)  
Malaganap na unemployment

**[09:26:27.480] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010049)  
at underemployment

**[09:26:29.160] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010050)  
dahil pinananatiling

**[09:26:32.140] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010051)  
atrasado ang

**[09:26:33.240] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010052)  
agrikultura at walang

**[09:26:35.260] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010053)  
sariling industriya.

**[09:26:37.820] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010054)  
Pareho, dahil ito

**[09:26:39.560] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010055)  
pinapaboran

**[09:26:40.680] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010056)  
ang importasyon

**[09:26:42.900] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010057)  
sa halip na sariling produksyon.

**[09:26:45.780] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010058)  
Service sector

**[09:26:47.140] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010059)  
jobs alone will not lead

**[09:26:49.120] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010060)  
to genuine growth.

**[09:26:51.020] Rep. Antonio L. Tinio** (asr-010061)  
Kung walang produksyon,
